title: 2003 HMMT February Calculus Problem 1
statement: A point is chosen randomly with uniform distribution in the interior of a circle of radius 1 . What is its expected distance from the center of the circle?

solutions.text:
\(2 / 3\)
The probability of the point falling between a distance \(r\) and \(r+d r\) from the center is the ratio of the area of the corresponding annulus to the area of the whole circle: \(\frac{\pi\left[(r+d r)^{2}-r^{2}\right]}{\pi} \rightarrow \frac{2 \pi r d r}{\pi}=2 r d r\) for small values of \(d r\). Then the expected distance is \(\int_{0}^{1} r \cot 2 r d r=\frac{2}{3}\).
